perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s available perspective:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. We work together but sometimes disagree about sales and marketing strategies.
- In a meeting room, I brought data and charts from our last five campaigns. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed traditional sales methods were being overlooked and could benefit our core sales more. I heard her say the market is evolving, that digital outreach has potential, and she asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement rates. I said I was not suggesting abandoning digital marketing, but was frustrated that proven traditional methods seemed sidelined without proper consideration. She said she understood my frustration and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that had boosted engagement and sales. I asked her to explain more about how those strategies are developed. She said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign. I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing the outcomes made me want to understand the digital approach more. She said she was glad I was open to exploring it and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- I felt uncertain, then hopeful. I proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital strategies. Katherine agreed, saying combining our strengths could lead to better results and suggesting we schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful that leveraging both our expertise could create something impactful and thanked her for collaborating. She said she looked forward to leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime on a draft presentation for the board that integrated our ideas. I told Katherine about the draft and my excitement. She reviewed it, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and said my hard work showed. I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors, and said I wanted to nail the presentation. She said she was confident with this preparation and suggested reviewing and fine-tuning it once more.
- After the presentation and implementation of the new strategy, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our successful collaboration. I told Katherine I could not thank her enough, that I had learned much from her, and that I was grateful for the growth our collaboration produced. She said it was a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition and that my openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership. I proposed regular strategy sessions to continue collaborating. She called it a fantastic idea and agreed, saying regular sessions would keep us on top of our game and market trends.

I have access to my own actions, feelings, and statements, and to what Katherine said and did in these interactions. I do not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, hidden motivations, her personality type, education, or any narrator-only details not expressed in our exchanges.
